findings.correction: Keep Im Kkeokjeong and add a first-use footnote: famous Joseon-era folk-hero bandit, hence the look-based nickname.
findings.current: However, he looked enough like a bandit that everyone called him Im Kkeokjeong.
findings.defect: First use of the unlisted nickname is romanized with no footnote. The joke and the reason everyone uses it depend on Im Kkeokjeong being the famous Korean folk-hero bandit, not a random hairy-man label.
findings.rationale: Binding footnote/ledger rule for unlisted names; without the namesake, the bandit appearance → 임꺽정 causal link is lost.
findings.source: 다만 산적을 연상시키는 외모라 모두 그를 임꺽정이라고 불렀다.

findings.defect: 거절 is an explicit rejection of the E-rank job, not a vague negative. “No” can read as disbelief or a one-word prompt rather than Taekyung trying to turn the contract down before the porter line.
findings.rationale: The next line (positions full; porter) answers a refusal. Softening 거절 to “No” changes the speech act.

findings.correction: “All right, everyone, say hello. This is a kid brother I know.”
findings.current: “All right, everyone, say hello. This is a younger brother of mine.”
findings.defect: Omits 아는 and makes 동생 sound like kinship. Source is a junior he knows, not a blood brother.
findings.rationale: Audit target is kinship. 아는 marks acquaintance; English “younger brother of mine” overstates the relationship.
findings.source: “자, 다들 인사해. 여긴 내 아는 동생.”

findings.correction:
Some people got angry, asking if this wasn’t just open discrimination.

It was.
findings.current:
Some people got angry and asked if the discrimination had to be so blatant.

It did.
findings.defect: Punchline confirms that it is discrimination, not that the blatancy “had to” exist.
findings.rationale: 차별하는 거 맞다 affirms the fact of discrimination; “It did” answers a different question.
findings.source: 너무 대놓고 차별하는 것 아니냐며 분노하는 사람도 있지만, 차별하는 거 맞다.

findings.correction: “Young man, you’re a tall one. You seem like you can fight.”
findings.current: “Young man, you’re quite a looker. You seem like you can fight.”
findings.defect: 훤칠하다 is tall, lanky, striking stature, not facial attractiveness. “Looker” breaks the link to looking like he can fight.
findings.rationale: Wrong physical attribute; the compliment is build/height, not being a looker.
findings.source: “젊은 친구가 훤칠하네. 잘 싸울 것 같어.”

findings.defect: Adds profanity. 이거 참 is a mild, embarrassed well-then, not a curse.
findings.rationale: Profanity must match source strength; this narration beat is not strong.

summary: Nickname, refusal, and kinship are the load-bearing misses: Im Kkeokjeong’s bandit-folk-hero force is unexplained, 거절 is reduced to a vague No, and 아는 동생 reads as blood family.
